new_findings.title: Extra permissive recovery-table policies can bypass verifier RLS checks
new_findings.defect: The validation loop at lines 159-167 checks only the named `operator_scope_{table}` policy, even though collection reads all policy rows. PostgreSQL combines permissive policies with OR, and no check rejects an additional permissive policy on an operator-scope table.
new_findings.failure_scenario: With ENABLE and FORCE RLS set and the approved `operator_scope_billing_reconciliation_cursor` intact, a `PUBLIC` policy `USING (true) WITH CHECK (true)` is added under another name. `collect_and_validate` still reports success, while an ordinary application database role with table privileges can read every seller-wide recovery row (and write rows if it has write privileges).
new_findings.fix: Validate all policies for each operator-scope table and fail on any unapproved permissive policy that broadens access; add a PostgreSQL regression case that keeps the approved policy and adds a second permissive `USING (true)` policy.

summary: The reported RLS omission is fixed and the lane unit suite passes, but an extra permissive policy can still make the verifier report healthy while exposing recovery rows; resolve this high-severity gap before merge.
